title: Traffic Reallocation Diary v1 (personal notes)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the next small-canary deployment (model v3.2 -> v3.3-lite) and an experiment to reallocate traffic by region. Not a polished runbook — this is my thinking-out-loud: constraints, hypotheses, and the minimal checklist I want in front of me during the run.

High-level goal:
- Safely shift 10% of US-west traffic to v3.3-lite for 4h window, measure P50/P95 latency, error-rate, and semantic similarity regressions on eval set. If green, bump to 30% and keep overnight.

Quick checklist (pre-deploy):
- Verify v3.3-lite health probes passing (ready/healthy for 2 consecutive cycles)
- Confirm KV-cache warming enabled on variant nodes
- Pin canary routing rule to model-tag:v3.3-lite-20260311
- Ensure fallback routing to v3.2 configured with <200ms decision timeout
- Create short-lived alerting group: pager -> oncall SRE, slack -> #canary-watch
- Snapshot baseline metrics (preceding 1h): tokens/sec, tail-latency, 5 golden prompts similarity scores

Traffic reallocation plan:
- Phase 1 (T+0): 1% traffic for 10m (sanity)
- Phase 2 (T+10m): 10% for 4h (primary observation window)
- Phase 3 (if green): 30% for 12h (overnight soak)
- Phase 4: roll forward to 100% with staged ramp if metrics steady

Safety triggers (immediate rollback):
- client_error_rate increases by >1 percentage point absolute in 15m
- 2x increase in model-timeout errors or 5xxs from serving nodes
- Mean similarity drift > 0.06 on eval set (quick sampled eval)
- Token-cost delta > +30% (unexpected compute regression)

Monitoring hooks to check (dashboard shortcuts):
- /dash/canary/latency (P50/P95/P99)
- /dash/canary/errors-by-code and by region
- /dash/canary/eval-similarity-live (automated runner output)
- Hosting CPU/GPU utilization and ROS spillover queue length

Version pinning notes:
- Use model tag, not image digest for now; pinned tag must include date+build id. Advantage: easier to correlate metrics. Disadvantage: potential tag reuse risk — double-check registry immutability.
- If pinning by digest: add manual mapping to release notes and create small ticket for ops to verify HSM KMS keys used for signing images.

Thoughts about staged rollouts across regions:
- Start in us-west only; reason: lower PG traffic impact, easier to isolate regional infra differences
- If we see region-specific regressions, divert remaining rollout to us-east and eu-west holdback cohorts
- Consider splitting model variant by hardware class: q4 (quantized) vs full fp16 — measure cost delta separately

Observations from previous micro-rollout (notes to self):
- KV-cache cold-start caused P95 spikes during early minutes; warmed after ~12m. Add warm-up traffic to nodes pre-route next time.
- A/B eval runner sometimes failed due to tokenization mismatch for older prompts (PR #891 fixed tokenizer edge-case)

Open questions / TODO:
- [ ] Should we enable automatic slow-fallback to a smaller context-length model if latency threshold exceeded? Pros/cons? (ask Priya)
- [ ] Confirm whether logs include model-output checksum by default (helps quick regression detection)
- [ ] Draft a tiny postmortem template for the canary window (if anything triggers)

Action items (my immediate next steps):
- Ping SRE oncall to reserve a 2h watch window tomorrow 09:30-11:30 PT
- Add 10 golden prompts to quick-eval runner and sanity-check tokenization
- Create ephemeral dashboard tile for 'similarity-by-prompt'
- Run a dry run in staging with identical routing rules and 5% synthetic traffic to simulate KV cache behavior

Quick heuristics I use while watching:
- If P95 > baseline + 20% but P50 is flat: likely edge-case/queueing; watch 10 more minutes before action
- If both P50 and P95 jump: lean toward rollback immediately (do not wait for 4h window)
- If only similarity drifts slightly (<0.02): sometimes model stochasticity; correlate with prompt-level logs before rollback

Last notes and logs I want appended after the run (template stub):
- run_start, run_end, phases timestamps
- metrics snapshot links (baseline and run)
- quick human summary (2 lines) and final decision (rollback/keep/roll-forward)
- follow-up tickets created and owner assigned

End of scratchpad. Will convert into a proper runbook if this pattern stabilizes after 2 successful canaries.

-- HS
